title: Torsion-controlled easy algebraization triples, direction into a completion
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal, $H$ a coherent module and $N\in\operatorname{Coh}(X,J)$, as in [pqf-def-locnoeth], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $\delta:N\to\widehat H_J$ have all component kernels and cokernels annihilated by one positive power of $J$. There exist a coherent $F$, a map $a:F\to H$, and $\beta:N\simeq\widehat F_J$ satisfying $\delta=\widehat a_J\circ\beta$. The actual coherent kernel and cokernel of $a$ are annihilated by one positive power of $J$. For every other such triple $(F',a',\beta')$ whose actual map $a'$ also has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a positive power of $J$, there exists exactly one isomorphism $\gamma:F\simeq F'$ with $a'\circ\gamma=a$ and $\widehat\gamma_J\circ\beta=\beta'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('it suffices to construct (F, a, beta) Zariski locally on X'); Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian) (2); Remark 0888

proof.text: Use the existing annihilation equivalence (conditions 1 and 2) to pass from componentwise annihilation to annihilation of the affine limit maps.
Apply the construction lemma to obtain one coherent triple with actual torsion kernel and cokernel and the desired comparison equation.

For a second torsion-controlled triple, form the completed comparison beta inverse followed by beta prime and its reverse. The two factorization equations imply that these commute with the completed arrows to H. Lift them by the unique-morphism-lifting lemma. Apply that same lemma to identity formal maps: uniqueness identifies the two composites with identities. These maps therefore define a coherent-module isomorphism. The forward lift equation gives the required beta equation. Any other compatible isomorphism has exactly the same completed map and arrow equation, so uniqueness of the morphism lift identifies its hom, and isomorphism extensionality identifies it.

lean.statement: theorem grothendieckExistenceEasy_torsionTriple {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J) (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H) (htorsion : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2 (kernel (δ.hom.app (op e)))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel (δ.hom.app (op e))))) : ∃ (F : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H) (β : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F), δ = β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a ∧ (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a.hom))) ∧ ∀ (F' : CoherentModules X) (a' : F' ⟶ H) (β' : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F'), δ = β'.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a' → (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (kernel a'.hom)) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a'.hom))) → ∃! γ : F ≅ F', γ.hom ≫ a' = a ∧ β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map γ.hom = β'.hom
